newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end up 0.84 pct on bonds, economy.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end up 0.84 pct on bonds, economy.

text.p: Argentina's blue-chip Merval stock index closed up 0.84 percent at 632.31 Tuesday, with the market bolstered by firmer bond prices and signs of economic recovery.
"The market has now digested the warning by the head of the (U.S.) Federal Reserve (Alan Greenspan) about stocks being overvalued," said one trader.
The Merval has risen 2.48 percent so far in December and by 13.0 percent over the past six weeks.
But Emilio Alessandro of Alessandro y Cia brokers said reported IMF concern over fiscal targets has tinged the market with caution.
"There has been some caution created among investors by the International Monetary Fund mission, which is analyzing the darker points of Argentina's fiscal performance," he said.
Alessandro said that stocks likely to benefit from economic recovery rose most strongly.
The market is also somewhat wary before Wednesday's U.S. inflation figures, said Gabriel Armando of Galicia Valores.
Thirty-four of the 69 stocks traded ended up, 14 lower and 21 shares closed unchanged.
The general share index closed 1.07 percent higher. Volume traded rose by 81 percent from Monday to $22 million.
Among the day's strongest performers were cement firm Juan Minetti and food company Molinos Rio de la Plata, both rising 3.07 percent.
The Merval closed 0.07 percent higher at 627 on Monday.
